vectors.name: minimal
vectors.description: EN-01 rule 2 — every zero-valued field omitted entirely. Only version, plane, domain, key_alg and priority are set, so the output must contain exactly five fields and nothing else.

vectors.name: forum-post-full
vectors.description: Every field populated, including a full anti-abuse block. The ordinary case.

vectors.name: anti-abuse-absent
vectors.description: EN-02 — an all-empty AntiAbuse is omitted entirely, never emitted as a zero-length message. Proto3 permits either shape; permitting both would be a second accepted form. This vector and 'anti-abuse-empty-object' MUST produce identical bytes.

vectors.name: anti-abuse-empty-object
vectors.description: Same as 'anti-abuse-absent' but with an explicitly-present, all-zero AntiAbuse. Must encode identically — that equality IS the rule.

vectors.name: anti-abuse-epoch-only
vectors.description: A single non-zero field inside the submessage — the submessage is emitted, but only that field within it.

vectors.name: large-timestamp
vectors.description: created_at_ms above 2^53. A double loses precision here, so this catches any consumer that routes an int64 through a float — the value is inside the signature.

vectors.name: bangla-broadcast
vectors.description: NFR-A04 — Bangla is a first-class locale, and SIG-26 budgets are computed against Bangla UTF-8 worst case. A normalisation divergence that only appears in the primary language of the target users is exactly what this gate exists to catch. Headline: 'পানি বাড়ছে, এখনই সরে যান' (water is rising, move now).

vectors.name: nfc-composed
vectors.description: EN-01 rule 4. This vector and 'nfc-decomposed' carry the same text in composed (U+00E9) and decomposed (U+0065 U+0301) form. After NFC normalisation they MUST produce identical bytes and therefore the identical content ID — otherwise the same post signed on two devices dedupes as two different objects.

vectors.name: nfc-decomposed
vectors.description: Decomposed twin of 'nfc-composed'. Identical expected output.

vectors.name: checkin-zero-cost
vectors.description: CR-01 — a check-in carries no credential and no PoW. This is the shape that must encode and verify when a person has zero credits, which is the whole point.

vectors.name: domain-separation-a
vectors.description: P0-G2 pair, half one. Identical to 'domain-separation-b' in every field except `domain`, so their canonical bytes and content IDs must differ. A signature over one must not verify the other.

vectors.name: domain-separation-b
vectors.description: P0-G2 pair, half two. Only `domain` differs from 'domain-separation-a'.

vectors.name: plane-separation-forum
vectors.description: P0-G3 pair, half one. Identical to 'plane-separation-signal' except for `plane`. Because the plane byte is inside the signature, a FORUM signature can never be lifted into a SIGNAL envelope (SEP-02).

vectors.name: plane-separation-signal
vectors.description: P0-G3 pair, half two. Only `plane` differs.

vectors.name: field-omission-sparse
vectors.description: P0-G4 pair, half one — THE v1 REGRESSION. A PostCreate body carrying only a title. v1 accepted a signature valid over either of two canonical forms, the legacy one omitting url, attachmentIds and poll, so a signature produced over exactly this body ALSO validated 'field-omission-populated' below — a post carrying an attacker-chosen URL and arbitrary attachments — and the verification UI showed a green check on the forgery.

vectors.name: field-omission-populated
vectors.description: P0-G4 pair, half two. Same title, plus an attacker-chosen url field. Canonical bytes and content ID MUST differ from 'field-omission-sparse', and a signature over one MUST NOT verify the other.
